title: Adaptogenic Latte: Your Secret Weapon to a Better Day
summary: Learn what adaptogenic lattes are, their health benefits for energy and focus, how they compare to coffee, and how to make one at home.
body_markdown:
An adaptogenic latte is your usual hot morning cup with adaptogens built in: plants and mushrooms that researchers study for helping your body maintain balance during stressful times. The world of adaptogens includes mushrooms, like lion's mane or chaga; roots, like maca or ginseng; and herbs, like tulsi.


## What Is an Adaptogenic Latte


An adaptogenic latte is a creamy hot drink built on a classic base: coffee, tea ([matcha](https://lairdsuperfood.com/blogs/news/(https://lairdsuperfood.com/products/matcha-instant-latte-with-adaptogens) or black), cacao, turmeric, or roasted roots (like chicory) with adaptogenic herbs or[functional mushrooms](https://lairdsuperfood.com/blogs/news/what-is-coffee-with-functional-mushrooms) brewed in. This base brew is topped with milk (dairy or nondairy), sweetened with a sweetener of choice, and served hot or over ice for an energizing, satisfying, and delicious daily ritual.


### How Adaptogens Work in the Body


Cortisol is the stress hormone your adrenal glands release, and it's the marker most adaptogen research keeps an eye on. Think of it as your body's built-in alarm: handy when you need it, but not something you want ringing all day. Adaptogens are there to help dial down that alarm. So when you pour a warm adaptogenic latte for yourself, it’s like a small, supportive pause in your day.


### What Different Adaptogens Are Known For


Each adaptogen has its own longstanding reputation. For example: maca is traditionally valued for energy; lion's mane is associated with mental clarity; ashwagandha is considered calming; and cordyceps has a reputation for increasing stamina and endurance.


### Energy, Focus, and Immunity in Every Sip


#### Energy


Caffeine from coffee, tea or cacao gives you the quick lift; adaptogens move you to a different energy plane altogether. Because they’re working with the body’s stress response, the energizing effects of adaptogens are felt over time. So while you’ll still get immediate energy from your latte if you’re sipping a caffeinated brew, it’s the long-term intake of adaptogenic lattes that gives you the most benefits when it comes to sustained energy throughout your day.


#### Focus


If your latte contains matcha, a green tea leaf powder, it naturally contains both caffeine and L-theanine, a compound that shows up alongside caffeine in the green tea leaf. In[trials](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12422004/) , caffeine paired with L-theanine improved attention and reduced mental fatigue.


Lion's mane, one of the most beloved functional mushrooms, is also valued for mental clarity. In a small 2023 study, healthy adults were faster on a[focus test](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10675414/) an hour after a single dose of Lion's mane. Human studies otherwise so far are small and short, with mixed results.


#### Immunity


Adaptogenic mushrooms, such as chaga, are being researched for their effects on the immune system, specifically through beta-glucans, fiber-like compounds found in mushrooms. Beta-glucans are studied for supporting the health of the immune tissue lining the gut, with research is still underway. Over 70% of the body's immune system sits in that tissue, so if immune support is what you want, look for chaga among the mushrooms named on the label.


## Caffeine: What to Expect in Your Cup


The caffeine content of an adaptogenic latte depends on the base. Coffee-based blends get their caffeine from the grounds, so a cup lands close to a regular cup of coffee, at about 95 mg per 8 oz cup.[Laird Superfood instant latte mixes](https://lairdsuperfood.com/collections/instant-lattes) carry about 100-120 mg per serving. Blends built on matcha (powdered green tea leaf) or cacao carry less, ranging from 20-90 mg per serving, and fully herbal blends carry none.


Choose a coffee- or matcha-based cup when you want a lift, and a caffeine-free cup later in the day.


## What Does an Adaptogenic Latte Taste Like


Just like a regular latte, an adaptogenic latte should provide a creamy and slightly sweet experience that’s as delicious as it is functional. The primary flavor will depend on whether your latte is coffee-, tea-, cacao-, or root-based, with this base ingredient doing the heavy lifting when it comes to flavor. The adaptogenic ingredients take a backseat, adding their own subtle flavor components without overwhelming the brew. For example: mushrooms will add an earthy, slightly mineral taste; maca comes with caramel-like, malty notes; ashwagandha has a hint of bitterness; and tulsi is warm and peppery. Depending on your preferences, you can dial up the latte flavor by finishing your cup with warming spices like cinnamon and ginger, or give it a treat-like vibe with vanilla or almond extract.

### Check In With Your Clinician First


Functional mushrooms and other adaptogens are an easy, relaxed addition for your daily routine, and a quick check-in keeps things smooth. Talk with your clinician before adding them if you:


- Are pregnant or breastfeeding
- Take prescription medication, such as blood thinners or immunosuppressants
- Have an ongoing health condition or surgery coming up


## FAQ


### How is an adaptogenic latte different from regular coffee?


Regular coffee gives you caffeine. An adaptogenic latte keeps the warm cup and adds functional mushrooms, roots, or herbs with adaptogenic properties.
